title.en: Volume 155 Biographies 80: Ma Sui and son: Chang, Hun Jian and son: Gao
title.raw: 卷一百五十五 列傳第八十 馬燧子:暢 渾瑊子:鎬 鐬 Volume 155 Biographies 80: Ma Sui and son: Chang, Hun Jian and son: Gao

sentences.zh: 馬燧馬燧，字洵美，系出右扶風，徙為汝州郟城人。

translations.literal: Ma Sui, Ma Sui, styled Xunmei, was of a lineage from right Fufeng and relocated to become a man of Jiaocheng in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui, styled Xunmei, traced his line to right Fufeng and had settled as a native of Jiaocheng in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 父季龍，舉孫吳倜儻善兵法科，仕至嵐州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ji Long passed the Sun-Wu Unconventional Talent Skilled in Military Methods examination and served up to prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji Long had passed the examination in Sun-Wu unconventional talent and skill in military methods, and rose to prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 燧姿度魁傑，長六尺二寸。

translations.literal: Sui's bearing was imposing and outstanding; his height was six feet two inches.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was imposing in stature and stood six feet two inches tall.

sentences.zh: 與諸兄學，輟策歎曰：「方天下有事，丈夫當以功濟四海，渠老一儒哉？

translations.literal: Studying with his elder brothers, he put down his book and sighed: "When the realm has affairs, a man ought to aid all under Heaven with merit — why grow old as a mere scholar?"
translations.idiomatic: While studying with his brothers, he laid aside his text and sighed: "The empire is in turmoil — a man should win merit to save the realm. Why waste away as a bookish recluse?"

sentences.zh: 」更學兵書戰策，沈勇多算。

translations.literal: He then studied military books and battle plans, deep in courage and abundant in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He turned instead to military texts and strategy, becoming deep in courage and rich in stratagem.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，使賈循守范陽。

translations.literal: An Lushan rebelled and sent Jia Xun to hold Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, he sent Jia Xun to hold Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 燧說循曰：「祿山首亂，今雖舉洛陽，猶將誅覆。

translations.literal: Sui persuaded Xun, saying: "Lushan began the rebellion; though he has now taken Luoyang, he will yet be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Sui urged Xun: "Lushan started this revolt. He may have seized Luoyang, but he is still headed for ruin."

sentences.zh: 公盍斬向潤客、牛廷玠！

translations.literal: Why do you not cut down Xiang Runkes and Niu Tingjie!
translations.idiomatic: Why not strike down Xiang Runkes and Niu Tingjie at once!

sentences.zh: 傾其本根，使西不得入關，退亡所據，則坐受禽矣，此不世功也。

translations.literal: Uproot their foundation so that he cannot enter the passes from the west; when he retreats with nowhere to stand, you will take him at ease — this is achievement not of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Cut out their root so he cannot force the passes from the west; when he retreats with nowhere to stand, you can take him at your leisure — a triumph for the ages.

sentences.zh: 」循許之，不時決。

translations.literal: Xun agreed but did not decide in time.
translations.idiomatic: Xun agreed, yet could not bring himself to act in time.

sentences.zh: 會顏杲卿招循舉兵，祿山遣韓朝陽召循計事，因縊殺之。

translations.literal: When Yan Gaoqing summoned Xun to raise troops, Lushan sent Han Chaoyang to summon Xun to consult on affairs and strangled him on the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Gaoqing called on Xun to raise arms, Lushan sent Han Chaoyang to summon him for counsel and had him strangled on the spot.

sentences.zh: 燧走西山，間道歸平原。

translations.literal: Sui fled to the western hills and by hidden paths returned to Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sui fled into the western hills and made his way back to Pingyuan by secret routes.

sentences.zh: 平原不守，復走魏。

translations.literal: Pingyuan could not be held; he fled again to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingyuan could no longer be held, he fled once more toward Wei.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，澤潞節度使李抱玉署為趙城尉。

translations.literal: In the Baoying era, Li Baoyu, military governor of Zelu, appointed him magistrate of Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying reign, Li Baoyu, military governor of Zelu, appointed him magistrate of Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 時回紇還國，恃功恣睢，所過皆剽傷，州縣供餼不稱，輒殺人。

translations.literal: At the time the Uyghurs were returning to their country, relying on merit and acting lawlessly; wherever they passed they plundered and harmed; when prefectures and counties failed to supply rations adequately they would kill people.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were then marching home, swaggering over their service; they looted and ravaged every district they crossed, and killed officials whenever local provisions fell short.

sentences.zh: 抱玉將饋勞，賓介無敢往，燧自請典辦具。

translations.literal: Baoyu was about to present gifts to reward them; none among the staff dared go; Sui volunteered to take charge of the provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu was preparing gifts to reward them, but none of his staff dared go near; Sui volunteered to oversee the supplies himself.

sentences.zh: 乃先賂其酋與約，得其旗章為信，犯令者得殺之。

translations.literal: He first bribed their chieftains and made agreements, obtaining their banner insignia as credentials; whoever violated orders could be killed.
translations.idiomatic: He first bribed their chiefs and bound them by agreement, taking their banner tokens as warrant to execute anyone who broke the rules.

sentences.zh: 燧又取死囚給役左右，小違令輒戮死，虜大駭，至出境，無敢暴者。

translations.literal: Sui also took condemned prisoners to serve at his side; the slightest violation of orders was immediately put to death; the barbarians were greatly terrified; by the time they reached the border, none dared act violently.
translations.idiomatic: Sui also took condemned men to serve at his side and had them executed for the least breach; the Uyghurs were terrified, and by the time they left the province none dared run wild.

sentences.zh: 抱玉才之。

translations.literal: Baoyu recognized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu came to value his ability.

sentences.zh: 因進說曰：「屬與回紇接，且得其情。

translations.literal: He therefore advanced and said: "Having recently dealt with the Uyghurs, I have come to understand their disposition."
translations.idiomatic: He then offered counsel: "I have just dealt with the Uyghurs and know their temper well."

sentences.zh: 觀僕固懷恩樹党自重，裂河北以授李懷仙、張忠志、薛嵩、田承嗣等，其子瑒佻勇不義，將必窺太原，公當備之。

translations.literal: Observing that Pugu Huai'en has built factions to magnify himself and partitioned Hebei to grant it to Li Huaixian, Zhang Zhongzhi, Xue Song, Tian Chengsi and others — his son Yang is frivolous, brave, and unrighteous — he will surely covet Taiyuan; Your Excellency should guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en has built a faction to magnify his power, carved up Hebei for Li Huaixian, Zhang Zhongzhi, Xue Song, Tian Chengsi, and the rest — and his son Yang is rash, bold, and unprincipled. He will surely eye Taiyuan. Your Excellency must prepare for that."

sentences.zh: 」既而懷恩與太原將謀舉其城，辛雲京覺之，不克。

translations.literal: Before long Huai'en and Taiyuan generals plotted to seize the city; Xin Yunjing discovered it and they did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huai'en and Taiyuan officers plotted to seize the city; Xin Yunjing uncovered the scheme and they failed.

sentences.zh: 嵩自相、衛歸懷恩糧，以絕河津。

translations.literal: Song transported grain from Xiang and Wei back to Huai'en, cutting off the river crossings.
translations.idiomatic: Song hauled grain from Xiang and Wei back to Huai'en, severing the river crossings.

sentences.zh: 抱玉令燧說嵩，嵩告絕於懷恩。

translations.literal: Baoyu ordered Sui to persuade Song; Song announced his break with Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu sent Sui to win over Song, and Song declared his break with Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 即署燧左武衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: He immediately appointed Sui military aide in the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He promptly appointed Sui military aide in the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 累進至鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By successive promotions he rose to prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 勸督農力，歲一稅，人以為便。

translations.literal: He urged and supervised agricultural effort; one tax per year — people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He urged and supervised farming, levying only one tax a year — a policy the people welcomed.

sentences.zh: 徙懷州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 時師旅後，歲大旱，田茀不及耕。

translations.literal: At the time, after armies had passed, the year saw severe drought; fields were overgrown and could not be cultivated in time.
translations.idiomatic: Armies had lately marched through the region, and a severe drought followed; fields lay choked with weeds and could not be plowed in season.

sentences.zh: 燧務勤教化，止橫調。

translations.literal: Sui devoted himself to promoting moral instruction and stopped arbitrary levies.
translations.idiomatic: Sui worked hard at moral instruction and put an end to arbitrary exactions.

sentences.zh: 將吏有親者，必造之，厚為禮。

translations.literal: Whenever officers or clerks had relatives, he would certainly visit them and treat them with generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an officer or clerk had kin in the district, he paid them a visit and treated them with generous courtesy.

sentences.zh: 瘞暴胔，止煩苛。

translations.literal: He buried exposed corpses and stopped vexatious severity.
translations.idiomatic: He buried the unburied dead and curbed petty harassment.

sentences.zh: 是秋，穭生於境，人賴以濟。

translations.literal: That autumn millet sprouted within his jurisdiction and the people were saved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn millet sprang up across his territory, and the people were saved by it.

sentences.zh: 抱玉守鳳翔，表燧隴州刺史。

translations.literal: Baoyu held Fengxiang and recommended Sui for prefect of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Baoyu held Fengxiang, he recommended Sui for prefect of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 西山直吐蕃，其上有通道，虜常所出入者。

translations.literal: The western mountains faced Tibet directly; above them was a pass by which the barbarians commonly entered and exited.
translations.idiomatic: The western hills faced Tibet directly, with a pass above that the enemy used constantly for raids.

sentences.zh: 燧聚石種樹障之，設二門為譙櫓，八日而畢，虜不能暴。

translations.literal: Sui amassed stones and planted trees to block it, set up two gates as watchtowers, and finished in eight days; the barbarians could not raid.
translations.idiomatic: Sui piled stone and planted trees to block the route, built two gate-towers as watch posts, and finished in eight days; the Tibetans could no longer raid through.

sentences.zh: 從抱玉入朝，代宗雅聞其才，召見，授商州刺史，兼水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: Following Baoyu to court, Emperor Daizong had long heard of his talent, summoned him for an audience, and appointed him prefect of Shangzhou and concurrently commissioner for water and land transport.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Baoyu to court, Emperor Daizong, who had long admired his ability, received him in audience and appointed him prefect of Shangzhou with concurrent charge of water and land transport.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，河陽兵逐其將常休明，詔燧檢校左散騎常侍，為三城使。

translations.literal: In the Dali era the He'yang troops expelled their commander Chang Xiuming; the emperor ordered Sui as acting Left Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary to serve as commissioner of the Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign the He'yang garrison drove out its commander Chang Xiuming; the court named Sui acting Left Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and commissioner of the Three Cities.

sentences.zh: 汴將李靈耀反，帝務息人，即授以汴宋節度留後，靈耀不拜，引魏博田承嗣為援。

translations.literal: The Bian commander Li Lingyao rebelled; the emperor seeking to spare the people immediately granted him the post of regent military governor of Bian-Song; Lingyao did not accept it and drew Tian Chengsi of Weibo as support.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian commander Li Lingyao rebelled; hoping to spare bloodshed, the emperor at once offered him the regency of Bian-Song — but Lingyao refused the post and called on Tian Chengsi of Weibo for aid.

sentences.zh: 詔燧與淮西李忠臣討之。

translations.literal: The court ordered Sui and Li Zhongchen of Huaixi to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Sui and Li Zhongchen of Huaixi to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 師次鄭，靈耀多張旗幟以犯王師，忠臣之兵潰而西。

translations.literal: The armies halted at Zheng; Lingyao deployed many banners to strike the imperial forces; Zhongchen's troops broke and fled westward.
translations.idiomatic: The armies halted at Zheng; Lingyao raised a forest of banners and struck the imperial column, and Zhongchen's force broke and fled west.

sentences.zh: 燧軍頓熒澤，鄭人震駭。

translations.literal: Sui's army encamped at Yingze; the people of Zheng were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's army encamped at Yingze, and the people of Zheng were stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 忠臣將遂歸，燧止之，益治軍，忠臣乃還收亡卒，復振。

translations.literal: Zhongchen was about to withdraw; Sui stopped him and further drilled the army; Zhongchen then returned to gather scattered troops and revived his force.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen was about to pull back; Sui held him, redoubled discipline in the ranks, and Zhongchen then rallied his scattered men and restored his army's morale.

sentences.zh: 忠臣行汴南，燧行汴北，敗賊于西梁固。

translations.literal: Zhongchen advanced on the south of Bian, Sui on the north of Bian, and they defeated the rebels at Xilianggu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen marched along the south bank of Bian, Sui along the north, and together they routed the rebels at Xilianggu.

sentences.zh: 靈耀以銳卒八千，號「餓狼軍」，燧獨戰破之，進至浚儀。

translations.literal: Lingyao had eight thousand crack troops styled the "Hungry Wolf Army"; Sui alone fought and broke them, advancing to Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyao fielded eight thousand elite troops he called the "Hungry Wolf Army"; Sui met them alone, shattered them, and pressed on to Junyi.

sentences.zh: 是時河陽兵冠諸軍，田悅帥眾二萬助靈耀，破永平將杜如江等，乘勝距汴一舍而屯。

translations.literal: At this time the He'yang army led all forces; Tian Yue commanded twenty thousand men to aid Lingyao, defeated the Yongping commander Du Rujiang and others, and following victory encamped one stage from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The He'yang army then outranked all others in the field; Tian Yue led twenty thousand men to Lingyao's aid, routed Yongping's Du Rujiang and his fellows, and following victory encamped a day's march from Bian.

sentences.zh: 忠臣合諸軍戰不利，燧為奇兵擊之，悅單騎遁，汴州平。

translations.literal: Zhongchen combined all armies but the battle went ill; Sui with extraordinary troops struck them; Yue fled on a single horse; Bianzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen joined all forces but the battle went badly; Sui struck with a flanking force, Yue fled alone on horseback, and Bianzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 燧知忠臣暴傲，讓其功，出舍板橋。

translations.literal: Sui knew Zhongchen was violent and arrogant, yielded the credit to him, and moved out to lodge at Banqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zhongchen's brutality and arrogance, Sui yielded him the credit and moved his quarters out to Banqiao.

sentences.zh: 忠臣入汴，果因會擊殺宋州刺史李僧惠。

translations.literal: Zhongchen entered Bian; sure enough at a gathering he struck and killed Li Senghui, prefect of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen entered Bian — and at a banquet, as Sui had foreseen, struck down Li Senghui, prefect of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 燧還河陽。

translations.literal: Sui returned to He'yang.
translations.idiomatic: Sui returned to He'yang.

sentences.zh: 秋大雨，河溢，軍吏請具舟以避，燧曰：「使城中盡魚而獨完其家，吾不忍。

translations.literal: In autumn great rains fell and the river overflowed; army officers asked to prepare boats to escape; Sui said: "To let everyone in the city become fish while my household alone remains intact — I cannot bear that."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn torrential rains swelled the river; his officers begged for boats to escape the flood. Sui said, "I cannot bear to see the whole city drowned while my household alone survives."

sentences.zh: 」既而水不為害。

translations.literal: Before long the water did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the waters subsided without harm.

sentences.zh: 遷河東節度留後，進節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regent military governor of Hedong, then advanced to full military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regent military governor of Hedong, then full military governor.

sentences.zh: 太原承鮑防之敗，兵力衰單，燧募廝役，得數千人，悉補騎士，教之戰，數月成精卒。

translations.literal: Taiyuan, bearing the aftermath of Bao Fang's defeat, had weakened and sparse forces; Sui recruited laborers and obtained several thousand, all supplemented as cavalrymen; he taught them warfare; in several months they became crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan still bore the sting of Bao Fang's defeat; its forces were thin. Sui recruited laborers by the thousands, enrolled them all as cavalry, drilled them in warfare, and within months had a corps of crack horsemen.

sentences.zh: 造鎧必短長三制，稱士所衣，以便進趨。

translations.literal: When making armor he always used three lengths, suited to each man's height, to facilitate advance and pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had armor made in three lengths to fit each man's stature, so troops could charge and pursue with ease.

sentences.zh: 為戰車，冒以狻猊象，列戟於後，行以載兵，止則為陣，遇險則制沖冒。

translations.literal: He made war chariots covered with lion imagery, with halberds arrayed behind; on the march they carried troops, at halt they formed battle lines, and in difficult terrain they served as assault vehicles.
translations.idiomatic: He built war chariots draped with lion figures, halberds ranked behind; on the march they carried troops, at rest they formed a battle line, and in rough ground they served as battering rams.

sentences.zh: 器用完銳。

translations.literal: Weapons were complete and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Every weapon was kept keen and ready.

sentences.zh: 居一年，辟廣場，羅兵三萬以肄，威震北方。

translations.literal: After a year he cleared a broad ground, arrayed thirty thousand troops for drill, and his might shook the north.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he cleared a broad parade ground, drew up thirty thousand men for drill, and his reputation shook the north.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，朝京師，遷檢校兵部尚書，封豳國公，還軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong he attended court in the capital, was promoted to acting Minister of War, enfeoffed as Duke of Bin, and returned to his army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong he came to court, was promoted acting Minister of War, enfeoffed Duke of Bin, and returned to his command.

sentences.zh: 初，田悅新有魏博，恐下未附，即輸款朝廷，燧建言悅必反。

translations.literal: Initially Tian Yue had newly acquired Weibo and feared his subordinates were not yet attached; he therefore submitted allegiance to the court; Sui advised that Yue would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yue had just seized Weibo and feared his men were not yet loyal, he sent tokens of submission to the court; Sui warned that Yue would surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 既而悅果圍邢州，身攻臨洺，築重城絕內外援。

translations.literal: Before long Yue indeed besieged Xingzhou, personally attacked Linming, and built layered ramparts to cut off internal and external aid.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yue did rebel, besieging Xingzhou and attacking Linming in person, raising layered walls to sever the cities from aid within and without.

sentences.zh: 邢將李洪、臨洺將張伾固守。

translations.literal: The Xing commander Li Hong and Linming commander Zhang Pi held fast in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong at Xing and Zhang Pi at Linming held their walls in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 詔燧以步騎二萬與昭義李抱真、神策兵馬使李晟合軍救之。

translations.literal: The court ordered Sui with twenty thousand foot and horse to join Li Baozhen of Zhaoyi and Shence army messenger Li Sheng in combined forces to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Sui with twenty thousand foot and horse to join Li Baozhen of Zhaoyi and Shence messenger Li Sheng in a combined relief force.

sentences.zh: 燧出𡻳口，未過險，移書抵悅，示之好。

translations.literal: Sui emerged from She Pass; before traversing the difficult terrain he sent a letter reaching Yue, showing goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Sui marched out through She Pass and, before crossing the difficult ground, sent Yue a letter feigning goodwill.

sentences.zh: 悅以燧畏己，大喜。

translations.literal: Yue thought Sui feared him and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yue took this as proof that Sui feared him and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 既次邯鄲，悅使至，燧皆斬之，遣兵破其支軍，射殺賊將成炫之。

translations.literal: Once they encamped at Handan, Yue's emissaries arrived; Sui executed them all, sent troops to break his detached army, and shot down the rebel general Cheng Xuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Handan, Yue's envoys came; Sui had them all beheaded, sent troops to rout his detached force, and shot down the rebel general Cheng Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 悅聞，使大將楊朝光以兵萬人據雙岡，築東西二柵以禦燧。

translations.literal: When Yue heard, he sent his great general Yang Chaoguang with ten thousand men to hold Shuanggang, building eastern and western palisades to resist Sui.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, Yue sent his chief general Yang Chaoguang with ten thousand men to hold Shuanggang and built eastern and western palisades to block Sui.

sentences.zh: 燧率軍營二壘間。

translations.literal: Sui led his army to encamp between the two fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Sui led his army to encamp between the two forts.

sentences.zh: 是夜，東壘遁，燧進營狗明山，取棄壘置輜重。

translations.literal: That night the eastern fortification fled; Sui advanced to encamp at Gouming Mountain, took the abandoned fort and stored baggage there.
translations.idiomatic: That night the eastern fort broke and fled; Sui advanced to Gouming Mountain, seized the abandoned works, and stored his baggage there.

sentences.zh: 悅計曰：「朝光堅柵，且萬人，雖燧能攻，未可以數日下，且殺傷必眾，則吾已拔臨洺，饗士以戰，必勝術也。

translations.literal: Yue calculated: "Chaoguang's palisades are strong and he has ten thousand men; though Sui can attack, it cannot be taken in a few days, and casualties will surely be heavy — then I will already have taken Linming, feast my troops and fight: this is the sure-win stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Yue reasoned: "Chaoguang's works are strong and he has ten thousand men. Even if Sui attacks, he cannot take them in days without heavy losses — by then I will have seized Linming, fed my troops, and struck: a certain path to victory."

sentences.zh: 」即分恒州兵五千助朝光。

translations.literal: He immediately divided five thousand Hengzhou troops to aid Chaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: He at once detached five thousand Hengzhou troops to reinforce Chaoguang.

sentences.zh: 燧令大將李自良等以騎兵守雙岡，戒曰：「令悅得過者斬！

translations.literal: Sui ordered his great generals Li Ziliang and others with cavalry to guard Shuanggang, warning: "If Yue gets through, beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Sui ordered his generals Li Ziliang and others to hold Shuanggang with cavalry, warning: "If Yue gets through, you die!"

sentences.zh: 」燧乃推火車焚朝光柵，自晨及晡，急擊，大破之，斬朝光，禽其將盧子昌，獲首五千，執八百人。

translations.literal: Sui then pushed fire carts to burn Chaoguang's palisades; from morning until afternoon he attacked fiercely, routed them thoroughly, beheaded Chaoguang, captured his general Lu Zichang, took five thousand heads, and seized eight hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Sui then drove fire-carts against Chaoguang's palisades and attacked fiercely from morning until afternoon, routing the position completely: Chaoguang was beheaded, his general Lu Zichang captured, five thousand heads taken, and eight hundred prisoners seized.

sentences.zh: 居五日，進軍臨洺。

translations.literal: After five days he advanced the army to Linming.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later he marched on Linming.

sentences.zh: 悅悉軍戰，燧自以銳士當之，凡百餘返，士皆決死，悅大敗，斬首萬級，俘系千余，館穀三十萬斛，邢圍亦解。

translations.literal: Yue committed his entire army to battle; Sui personally took crack troops to meet them; they clashed over a hundred times; the soldiers were all resolved to die; Yue was utterly defeated — ten thousand heads cut, over a thousand captured and bound, thirty thousand bushels of grain in stores, and the siege of Xing was also lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Yue threw his whole army into the fight; Sui himself led crack troops against them in more than a hundred charges; every man fought as if resolved to die; Yue was utterly routed — ten thousand heads taken, more than a thousand prisoners bound, thirty thousand bushels of grain captured, and the siege of Xing was lifted as well.

sentences.zh: 以功遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，將戰，燧約眾，勝則以家貲賞。

translations.literal: Before the battle Sui had made a covenant with the troops: if victorious he would reward them with his household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Before the battle Sui had promised his men that if they won, he would reward them from his private fortune.

sentences.zh: 至是，殫私財賜麾下。

translations.literal: At this point he exhausted his private wealth in gifts to his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Now he emptied his private wealth in gifts to his command.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，詔出度支錢五千萬償其財。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong commended him and ordered five million from the treasury to reimburse his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong praised him and ordered five million from the treasury to make good his losses.

sentences.zh: 進兼魏博招討使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to concurrent Commissioner for Suppressing and Pacifying Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed concurrent Commissioner for Suppressing and Pacifying Weibo.

sentences.zh: 李納、李惟岳合兵萬三千人救悅，悅裒散兵二萬壁洹水，淄青軍其左，恒冀軍其右。

translations.literal: Li Na and Li Weiyue combined thirteen thousand men to rescue Yue; Yue gathered twenty thousand scattered troops to fortify at the Huan River; the Ziqing army on his left, the Hengji army on his right.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na and Li Weiyue joined forces with thirteen thousand men to relieve Yue; Yue rallied twenty thousand scattered troops and fortified along the Huan River, with the Ziqing army on his left and the Hengji army on his right.

sentences.zh: 燧進屯鄴，請益兵。

translations.literal: Sui advanced to encamp at Ye and requested additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sui advanced to encamp at Ye and asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 詔河陽李芃以兵會，次於漳。

translations.literal: The court ordered Li Pang of He'yang to join with troops; they halted at Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Li Pang of He'yang to join him with troops; they halted at Zhang.

sentences.zh: 悅遣將王光進以兵守漳之長橋，築月壘扼軍路。

translations.literal: Yue sent his general Wang Guangjin with troops to hold the long bridge at Zhang, building crescent ramparts to choke the army's route.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Wang Guangjin to hold the long bridge on the Zhang with crescent ramparts that blocked the imperial line of march.

sentences.zh: 燧於下流以鐵鏁維車數百絕河，載土囊遏水而後度。

translations.literal: Sui downstream used iron chains linking hundreds of carts to block the river, loaded earth bags to hold back the water, and then crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Downstream Sui chained hundreds of wagons with iron links to dam the river, piled earth bags to hold back the current, and then crossed.

sentences.zh: 悅知燧食乏，深壁不戰。

translations.literal: Yue knew Sui's food was scarce and deeply fortified without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yue knew Sui's supplies were running low and dug in behind strong walls, refusing battle.

sentences.zh: 燧令士齎十日糧，進營倉口，與悅夾洹而軍，造三橋逾洹，日挑戰。

translations.literal: Sui ordered the soldiers to carry ten days' rations, advanced to encamp at Cangkou, faced Yue across the Huan, built three bridges to cross the Huan, and provoked battle daily.
translations.idiomatic: Sui had his men carry ten days' rations, advanced to Cangkou, faced Yue across the Huan, threw three bridges across the river, and taunted him to fight every day.

sentences.zh: 悅不出，陰伏萬人，將以掩燧。

translations.literal: Yue did not emerge but secretly hid ten thousand men intending to surprise Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yue would not come out, but secretly hid ten thousand men to ambush Sui.

sentences.zh: 燧令諸軍夜半食，先雞鳴時鳴鼓角，而潛師並洹趨魏州，令曰：「聞賊至，止為陣。

translations.literal: Sui ordered all armies to eat at midnight; before cockcrow to sound drums and horns while secretly moving troops along the Huan toward Weizhou, with the order: "If you hear the enemy coming, halt and form battle lines only."
translations.idiomatic: Sui ordered the armies to eat at midnight, sound drums and horns before cockcrow, and secretly march along the Huan toward Weizhou, with the command: "If you hear the enemy, stop and form ranks only."

sentences.zh: 」留百騎持火，待軍畢發，匿其旁，須悅眾度，即焚橋。

translations.literal: He left a hundred cavalry holding fire; when the army had fully departed they would hide beside the route; when Yue's masses had crossed they would burn the bridges.
translations.idiomatic: He left a hundred horsemen with torches to wait until the main body had gone, then lie in hiding; once Yue's forces had crossed, they were to burn the bridges.

sentences.zh: 燧行十餘里，悅率李納等兵逾橋，乘風縱火，噪而前。

translations.literal: Sui had marched more than ten li when Yue led Li Na and others' troops across the bridge, riding the wind to spread fire, shouting as they advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Sui had marched more than ten li when Yue led Li Na and the rest across the bridges, fanning the flames with the wind and charging forward with a great clamor.

sentences.zh: 燧乃令士無動，命除榛莽廣百步為場，募勇士五千人陣而待。

translations.literal: Sui then ordered the soldiers not to move, commanded clearing brambles for a hundred paces as a field, recruited five thousand brave warriors to form lines and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Sui ordered his men to hold still, had brush cleared for a hundred paces to make a field, and mustered five thousand picked warriors in battle order to receive them.

sentences.zh: 比悅至，火止，氣少衰，燧縱兵擊之，悅敗走橋，橋已焚，眾赴水死者不可計，斬首二萬級，殺賊將孫晉卿、安墨啜，虜三千人，屍相駘藉三十里，淄青兵幾殲。

translations.literal: By the time Yue arrived the fire had stopped and their spirit had somewhat waned; Sui unleashed his troops upon them; Yue was defeated and fled toward the bridge — the bridges were already burned; masses drowned in the water beyond counting — twenty thousand heads cut, rebel generals Sun Jinqing and An Mochuo killed, three thousand captured, corpses piled for thirty li, and the Ziqing army was nearly annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Yue arrived the fires had died and his men's ardor had faded; Sui loosed his troops on them. Yue was routed and fled for the bridges — but they were already burning. Countless men drowned in the river; twenty thousand heads were taken, the rebel generals Sun Jinqing and An Mochuo were killed, three thousand captured, and corpses lay heaped for thirty li — the Ziqing army was nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 悅夜走魏州，其將拒不納，比明，追不至，悅乃得入。

translations.literal: Yue fled by night toward Weizhou; his generals refused to admit him; by dawn pursuers had not caught him, and only then did Yue gain entry.
translations.idiomatic: Yue fled by night toward Weizhou; his own officers at first refused him entry; by dawn the pursuers had not caught him, and only then did he slip inside the city.

sentences.zh: 抱真、芃問曰：「糧少而深入，何也？

translations.literal: Baozhen and Pang asked: "With little grain yet advancing deep — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen and Pang asked him: "Your supplies were scant — why did you drive so deep into enemy country?"

sentences.zh: 」燧曰：「糧少戰利速，兵善於致人。

translations.literal: Sui said: "With little grain, quick victory profits us; troops excel at bringing the enemy to them."
translations.idiomatic: Sui replied: "Scant rations make for swift victory, and good troops excel at drawing the enemy out."

sentences.zh: 今悅與淄青、恒三軍為首尾，欲不戰以老我師。

translations.literal: Now Yue with the Ziqing and Heng armies form head and tail, wishing not to fight so as to wear down our army.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and the Ziqing and Heng armies now form a single front; they mean to avoid battle and wear our force down."

sentences.zh: 若分擊左右，未可必破，悅且來助，是腹背支敵也。

translations.literal: If we divide to strike left and right, we cannot be sure of breaking them; Yue will come to aid — that is enemies on belly and back.
translations.idiomatic: If we split to strike their flanks, we cannot be sure of breaking either wing, and Yue will come to their aid — we would face enemies before and behind."

sentences.zh: 法有攻其必救，故趨魏以破之。

translations.literal: In military law there is attacking what they must rescue; therefore I rushed on Wei to break them.
translations.idiomatic: The classic rule is to strike what the enemy must relieve — that is why I marched on Wei to break them."

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「善。

translations.literal: All said: "Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: They all agreed that he was right.

sentences.zh: 悅嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Yue surrounded himself within the city and held it in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yue shut himself inside the city walls and held on.

sentences.zh: 於是李再春以博州、悅兄昂以洛州、王光進以長橋皆降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Zaichun with Bozhou, Yue's elder brother Ang with Luozhou, and Wang Guangjin with the long bridge all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Zaichun surrendered Bozhou, Yue's elder brother Ang Luozhou, and Wang Guangjin the long bridge — all came over.

sentences.zh: 悅使符璘、李瑤衛還淄青殘兵，璘等亦降。

translations.literal: Yue sent Fu Lin and Li Yaowei to escort the remnant Ziqing troops back; Lin and the others also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Fu Lin and Li Yaowei to escort the battered Ziqing troops home; they too surrendered.

sentences.zh: 魏導禦溝貫城，燧塞其上游，魏人恐。

translations.literal: Wei had a defensive moat running through the city; Sui blocked its upper reaches and the people of Wei were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: A defensive canal ran through Wei; Sui dammed its upper course, and the city was stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 悅遣許士則、侯臧間行告窮於硃滔、王武俊，會二人者怨望，乃連和。

translations.literal: Yue sent Xu Shize and Hou Zang by secret routes to report his straits to Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun; as it happened both men harbored grievances, and they therefore joined in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Xu Shize and Hou Zang by secret paths to beg help from Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun; both men were nursing grievances against the court, and they now joined forces with him.

sentences.zh: 悅恃燕、趙方至，即出兵背城陣，燧復與諸軍破之。

translations.literal: Yue relied on the Yan and Zhao forces having just arrived and immediately sent troops to form a battle line with their backs to the city; Sui again joined the armies and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Counting on the Yan and Zhao reinforcements that had just arrived, Yue marched out and drew up a line with the city at his back; Sui and the allied armies routed him again.

sentences.zh: 進同中書門下平章事、北平郡王、魏州大都督長史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, King of Beiping commandery, and chief administrator of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Grand Councilor, enfeoffed King of Beiping, and made chief administrator of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 滔、武俊聯兵五萬傅魏。

translations.literal: Tao and Wujun combined fifty thousand troops and pressed on Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Tao and Wujun joined fifty thousand men and closed on Wei.

sentences.zh: 會帝遣李懷光以朔方軍萬五千助燧。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Li Huai'guang with fifteen thousand Shuofang troops to aid Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Li Huai'guang with fifteen thousand Shuofang troops to reinforce Sui.

sentences.zh: 懷光勇於鬥，未休士，即與滔等戰，不利。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was bold in battle; without resting the troops he immediately fought Tao and the others and fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang was eager for a fight; without giving his men rest he engaged Tao and the rest at once and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 悅決水灌軍，燧兵亦屈，退保魏縣。

translations.literal: Yue breached the dikes to flood the army; Sui's troops were also checked and withdrew to defend Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Yue broke the dikes to inundate the imperial camp; Sui's force was driven back as well and withdrew to hold Weixian.

sentences.zh: 滔等瀕河為壘。

translations.literal: Tao and the others built ramparts along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Tao and his allies threw up ramparts along the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 會涇師亂，帝幸奉天，燧還軍太原。

translations.literal: The Jingzhou troops mutinied; the emperor went to Fengtian; Sui returned his army to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingzhou garrison mutinied and the emperor fled to Fengtian, Sui marched his army back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，李抱真欲殺懷州刺史楊鉥，鉥奔燧，燧奏其非罪，乃免。

translations.literal: Initially Li Baozhen wished to kill Yang Shu, prefect of Huaizhou; Shu fled to Sui; Sui memorialized that he was not guilty and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Baozhen had wanted to execute Yang Shu, prefect of Huaizhou; Shu fled to Sui, who pleaded that he was innocent, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 抱真怒。

translations.literal: Baozhen was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen was furious.

sentences.zh: 及共解邢圍，獲軍糧，燧自有之，以餘給抱真軍，抱真益怒。

translations.literal: When together they lifted the siege of Xing and captured army grain, Sui kept it for himself and gave only the remainder to Baozhen's army; Baozhen grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: When they together relieved Xing and seized army stores, Sui kept the bulk for himself and gave Baozhen only the leavings — and Baozhen's resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 洹之捷，軍進薄魏，悅以突騎犯燧營，李芃救之，抱真勒兵不出。

translations.literal: After the victory at the Huan, the army advanced close to Wei; Yue with shock cavalry struck Sui's camp; Li Pang rescued him; Baozhen held his troops back and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory on the Huan the armies pressed Wei; Yue's shock cavalry hit Sui's camp, Li Pang rode to the rescue, but Baozhen held his men back and would not move.

sentences.zh: 燧將攻魏，取攻具于抱真營，並請雜兩軍平其功，抱真不聽，請獨當一面，繇是逗遛。

translations.literal: When Sui was about to attack Wei he took siege equipment from Baozhen's camp and also asked to mix the two armies to share the merit equally; Baozhen would not agree and asked to hold one front alone; from this they delayed.
translations.idiomatic: As Sui prepared to assault Wei he took siege engines from Baozhen's camp and asked to blend both armies so credit would be shared; Baozhen refused and demanded a separate front — and from that moment the campaign stalled.

sentences.zh: 帝數遣使講解。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to mediate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent mediator after mediator, to no avail.

sentences.zh: 武俊略趙地，抱真分麾下二千人戍邢，燧怒謂：「抱真以兵還守其地，我能獨戰死邪？

translations.literal: Wujun overran Zhao territory; Baozhen detached two thousand men under his command to garrison Xing; Sui angrily said: "Baozhen sends troops back to guard his own territory — am I to fight and die alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Wujun overran Zhao; Baozhen peeled off two thousand of his men to garrison Xing. Sui raged: "He pulls his troops back to guard his own ground — am I supposed to fight and die alone?"

sentences.zh: 」將引還，李晟和之，乃復與抱真善。

translations.literal: He was about to withdraw; Li Sheng reconciled them, and he again became friendly with Baozhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of pulling out when Li Sheng patched things up, and the two were on good terms again.

sentences.zh: 及田昂降，燧請以洺州隸抱真，而用昭義副使盧玄卿為刺史，兼魏博招討副使。

translations.literal: When Tian Ang surrendered, Sui requested that Linming be placed under Baozhen and that Zhaoyi deputy commissioner Lu Xuanqing be made prefect, concurrently deputy commissioner for suppressing Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Ang surrendered, Sui asked that Linming be assigned to Baozhen, with Zhaoyi deputy Lu Xuanqing as prefect and his own deputy in the Weibo campaign.

sentences.zh: 李晟兵前獨隸抱真，抱真亦請兼隸於燧，以示協一。

translations.literal: Li Sheng's troops had earlier been solely under Baozhen; Baozhen also asked that they be jointly under Sui, to show unity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng's force had reported only to Baozhen; Baozhen now asked that it answer jointly to Sui as well, as a gesture of unity.

sentences.zh: 然議者咎燧私忿交惡，卒不成大功。

translations.literal: Yet commentators blamed Sui for private resentment and mutual enmity, and in the end he did not achieve great success.
translations.idiomatic: Critics blamed Sui's private feuds for the failure to finish the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 至太原，遣軍司馬王權以兵五千走奉天，又遣子匯與諸將子壁中渭橋，帝已幸梁，乃還。

translations.literal: On reaching Taiyuan he sent army marshal Wang Quan with five thousand troops to hurry to Fengtian, and also sent his son Hui with generals' sons to fortify the central Wei Bridge; the emperor had already gone to Liang, and they then returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan he sent army marshal Wang Quan with five thousand men racing to Fengtian, and his son Hui with other generals' sons to hold the central Wei Bridge — but the emperor had already fled to Liang, so they turned back.

sentences.zh: 時天下方騷，北邊數有警，燧念晉陽王業所基，宜固險以示敵。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was in turmoil and the northern frontier had repeated alarms; Sui reflected that Jinyang was the foundation of royal enterprise and ought to be fortified by difficult terrain to show the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was in uproar and the northern frontier alarm after alarm; Sui judged that Jinyang, foundation of the Tang house, must be made defensible and daunting to any foe.

sentences.zh: 乃引晉水架汾而屬之城，瀦為東隍，省守陴萬人。

translations.literal: He therefore diverted the Jin River, bridged it over the Fen and linked it to the city, dammed it as an eastern moat, and reduced wall-guards by ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He diverted the Jin River, carried it over the Fen on aqueducts into the city, impounded an eastern moat, and cut ten thousand men from the wall garrison.

sentences.zh: 又釃汾環城，樹以固堤。

translations.literal: He also channeled the Fen to encircle the city and planted trees to strengthen the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: He also ringed the city with the Fen and planted trees along the embankments to hold them firm.

sentences.zh: 詔兼保甯軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve concurrently as military governor of the Baoning Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named concurrent military governor of the Baoning Army.

sentences.zh: 帝還京，李懷光反河中，詔燧為河東保寧、奉誠軍行營副元帥，與渾瑊、駱元光合兵討之。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong; Sui was ordered as deputy supreme commander of the Hedong Baoning and Fengcheng campaign armies, and joined Hun Jian and Luo Yuanguang in combined forces to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Chang'an, Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong; Sui was named deputy supreme commander of the eastern campaign and joined Hun Jian and Luo Yuanguang to crush him.

sentences.zh: 時賊黨要廷珍守晉、毛朝易攵守隰、鄭抗守慈，燧移檄鐫諭，皆以州降，因拜燧晉絳慈隰節度使。

translations.literal: At the time the rebel party held Jin with Yao Tingzhen, Xi with Mao Chaoai, and Ci with Zheng Kang; Sui sent proclamations engraved to instruct them, and all surrendered their prefectures; he was therefore appointed military governor of Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel holdouts still guarded Jin under Yao Tingzhen, Xi under Mao Chaoai, and Ci under Zheng Kang; Sui's written appeals brought them all over, and he was appointed military governor of Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 武俊之圍趙也，康日知不支，將棄趙，燧請詔武俊擊硃滔，授以深、趙，以日知為晉慈隰節度使。

translations.literal: When Wujun besieged Zhao, Kang Rizhi could not hold out and was about to abandon Zhao; Sui requested an edict ordering Wujun to attack Zhu Tao, granting him Shen and Zhao, and making Rizhi military governor of Jin, Ci, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wujun besieged Zhao and Kang Rizhi was near collapse, Sui proposed that the court order Wujun against Zhu Tao, reward him with Shen and Zhao, and give Rizhi the Jin-Ci-Xi command.

sentences.zh: 及三州降，燧固讓日知，且言因降受節，恐後有功者踵以為利，帝嘉許。

translations.literal: When the three prefectures surrendered, Sui firmly yielded to Rizhi and moreover said that receiving a command for surrender might encourage later men of merit to follow for profit; the emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: When the three prefectures came over, Sui firmly yielded the post to Rizhi, warning that rewarding surrender with a command might teach future generals to trade capitulation for office — and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 籍府庫兵仗以授日知，日知大喜過望。

translations.literal: He inventoried the treasury and armory and handed them to Rizhi; Rizhi was delighted beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He turned over the treasury rolls and armories to Rizhi, who was overwhelmed with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 燧乃率步騎三萬次於絳，略定諸縣，降其將馮萬興、任象玉，遂圍絳，拔外郛，守將夜棄城去，降四千人。

translations.literal: Sui then led thirty thousand foot and horse to encamp at Jiang, pacified the various counties, received the surrender of his generals Feng Wanxing and Ren Xiangyu, then besieged Jiang, took the outer wall, the defending commander abandoned the city by night and fled, and four thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sui marched thirty thousand foot and horse to Jiang, swept the surrounding counties, and won over Feng Wanxing and Ren Xiangyu; he then invested Jiang, took the outer suburbs, and when the garrison fled by night four thousand men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遣李自良定六縣，降其將辛兟，收卒五千。

translations.literal: He sent Li Ziliang to pacify six counties, received the surrender of the general Xin E, and gathered five thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Ziliang to secure six counties, won over the general Xin E, and enrolled five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 裨將谷秀違令掠士女，斬以徇。

translations.literal: The lieutenant Gu Xiu violated orders and plundered men and women; he was beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant Gu Xiu had defied orders and looted civilians; Sui had him beheaded as an example.

sentences.zh: 與賊戰寶鼎，射殺賊將徐伯文，斬首萬級，獲馬五百。

translations.literal: Fighting the rebels at Baoding, he shot and killed the rebel general Xu Bowen, cut ten thousand heads, and captured five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: At Baoding he met the rebels, shot down their general Xu Bowen, took ten thousand heads, and seized five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 于時天下蝗，兵艱食，物貨翔踴，中朝臣多請宥懷光者，帝未決。

translations.literal: At the time locusts plagued the realm, troops had scarce food, goods soared in price, and many court ministers asked to pardon Huai'guang; the emperor had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged the land, armies went hungry, prices soared, and many at court urged clemency for Huai'guang — but the emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 燧以「懷光逆計久，反覆不可信。

translations.literal: Sui argued that "Huai'guang's rebellious designs are of long standing and his reversals cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Sui argued that "Huai'guang has plotted rebellion for years and cannot be trusted to keep his word."

sentences.zh: 河中近甸，舍之屈威靈，無以示天下，」乃舍軍入朝，為天子自言之：「且得三十日糧，足平河中。

translations.literal: Hezhong is near the capital domain; to spare him would humble imperial majesty and give no sign to all under Heaven." He therefore left the army and entered court, speaking for himself to the Son of Heaven: "Give me thirty days' grain and that suffices to pacify Hezhong."
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong lies on the capital's doorstep; to let him off would humble the throne before the world." He left his army and went to court in person: "Give me thirty days' provisions and I will finish Hezhong."

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃與瑊、元光、韓遊瑰之兵合。

translations.literal: He then combined with the armies of Jian, Yuanguang, and Han Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: He then united his force with those of Hun Jian, Luo Yuanguang, and Han Yougui.

sentences.zh: 賊將徐廷光守長春宮城。

translations.literal: The rebel general Xu Tingguang held Changchun Palace city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Xu Tingguang held Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 燧度長春不下，則懷光固守，久攻所傷必眾，乃挺身至城下見廷光。

translations.literal: Sui judged that if Changchun were not taken, Huai'guang would hold fast; a long siege would surely cost many casualties; he therefore went in person to the foot of the wall to see Tingguang.
translations.idiomatic: Sui reckoned that unless Changchun fell, Huai'guang would dig in and a long siege would bleed his army dry — so he walked alone to the wall and called on Tingguang.

sentences.zh: 廷光憚燧威，拜城上。

translations.literal: Tingguang feared Sui's authority and bowed from atop the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Tingguang, in awe of Sui's reputation, bowed from the battlements.

sentences.zh: 燧顧其心已屈，徐曰：「我自朝廷來，可西向受命。

translations.literal: Sui saw that his heart was already bent and said slowly: "I come from the court — you may face west to receive command."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his will already broken, Sui said gently: "I bear the court's commission — face west and receive your orders."

sentences.zh: 」廷光再拜。

translations.literal: Tingguang bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Tingguang bowed low twice.

sentences.zh: 燧曰：「公等朔方士，自祿山以來，功高天下，奈何棄之為族滅計？

translations.literal: Sui said: "You gentlemen are Shuofang men; since the time of Lushan your merit has towered over the realm — why cast it away for a plan that will exterminate your clans?"
translations.idiomatic: Sui said: "You are Shuofang soldiers — since An Lushan's day your service has outshone the realm. Why throw that away on a course that will destroy your families to the last man?"

sentences.zh: 若從吾言，非止免禍，富貴可遂也。

translations.literal: If you follow my words, you will not only escape calamity — wealth and honor may be secured as well.
translations.idiomatic: Heed me and you will not merely escape ruin — wealth and rank can still be yours."

sentences.zh: 」未對，燧曰：「爾以吾為欺邪？

translations.literal: He did not answer; Sui said: "Do you take me for a deceiver?"
translations.idiomatic: When he did not answer, Sui said: "Do you think I am lying to you?"

sentences.zh: 今不遠數步，可射我。

translations.literal: I am but a few paces away — you may shoot me now.
translations.idiomatic: I stand only a few steps away — shoot me if you doubt me."

sentences.zh: 」披而示之心。

translations.literal: He opened his robe and showed his breast.
translations.idiomatic: He opened his robe and bared his chest to them.

sentences.zh: 廷光感泣，一軍皆流涕，即率眾降。

translations.literal: Tingguang wept with emotion; the whole army streamed with tears and immediately led the masses in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tingguang wept; the whole garrison wept with him, and he led them out in surrender at once.

sentences.zh: 燧以數騎入其城，眾大呼曰：「吾等更為王人矣！

translations.literal: Sui entered their city with a few horsemen; the masses shouted loudly: "We are again men of the king!"
translations.idiomatic: Sui rode into the city with only a few escorts; the men shouted: "We are the emperor's soldiers again!"

sentences.zh: 」渾瑊亦自以為不及也，歎曰：「嘗疑馬公能窘田悅，今觀其制敵，固有過人者，吾不逮遠矣！

translations.literal: Hun Jian also considered himself inferior and sighed: "I once doubted that Lord Ma could corner Tian Yue; now seeing how he masters the enemy, he truly has what surpasses others — I fall far short!"
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian judged himself outclassed and sighed: "I used to wonder whether Lord Ma could truly corner Tian Yue — but watching him master an enemy, I see gifts I lack by a wide margin."

sentences.zh: 進營焦籬堡，堡將降，餘戍望風遁去。

translations.literal: He advanced to encamp at Jiaoli Fort; the fort commander surrendered and the remaining garrisons fled at the rumor of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Jiaoli Fort; its commander surrendered, and the other posts fled before his approach.

sentences.zh: 燧濟河，兵八萬陣城下。

translations.literal: Sui crossed the river; eighty thousand troops arrayed beneath the city.
translations.idiomatic: Sui crossed the river and drew up eighty thousand men beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊將牛名俊斬懷光降，眾猶萬六千。

translations.literal: That day the rebel general Niu Mingjun beheaded Huai'guang and surrendered; the masses still numbered sixteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the rebel general Niu Mingjun killed Huai'guang and came over, with sixteen thousand men still under arms.

sentences.zh: 誅其党閻晏、孟寶、張清、吳冏等，它脅附悉赦之。

translations.literal: His faction Yan Yan, Meng Bao, Zhang Qing, Wu Jiong and others were executed; all others coerced into following were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: His hard-core followers Yan Yan, Meng Bao, Zhang Qing, Wu Jiong, and the rest were put to death; everyone else who had been forced along was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 不閱月，河中平。

translations.literal: Within less than a month Hezhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month Hezhong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿大夫，兼侍中，賜一子五品官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and concurrent Palace Attendant; one son was granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and concurrent Palace Attendant, and one son was given a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 還太原，帝賜《宸扆》、《台衡》二銘，以言君臣相成之美。

translations.literal: Returning to Taiyuan, the emperor bestowed two inscriptions, "Imperial Screen" and "Pillar and Scale," speaking of the beauty of ruler and minister completing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Taiyuan, the emperor gave him two commemorative texts, "Imperial Screen" and "Pillar and Scale," praising the harmony of throne and servant.

sentences.zh: 勒石起義堂，帝榜其顏以寵之。

translations.literal: He carved them in stone at the Hall of Righteous Uprising; the emperor inscribed the heading in his own hand as a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: The texts were carved in stone at the Hall of Righteous Uprising, with the emperor's own brush for the title as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，吐蕃尚結贊破鹽、夏二州，守之，自屯鳴沙。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan the Tibetan Shang Jiezan captured Yan and Xia prefectures, held them, and himself encamped at Mingsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan the Tibetan commander Shang Jiezan took Yan and Xia, garrisoned them, and camped at Mingsha.

sentences.zh: 及春，畜產死，糧乏。

translations.literal: When spring came their livestock died and grain was scarce.
translations.idiomatic: By spring their herds were dying and provisions ran short.

sentences.zh: 詔燧為綏銀麟勝招討使，與駱元光、韓遊瑰等會師擊虜。

translations.literal: Sui was ordered Commissioner for Suppressing and Pacifying Sui, Yin, Lin, and Sheng, and joined Luo Yuanguang, Han Yougui and others in combined armies to strike the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was named commissioner to suppress the frontier and joined Luo Yuanguang, Han Yougui, and others to strike the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 燧次石州。

translations.literal: Sui encamped at Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sui halted at Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 結贊懼，乞盟，帝不許。

translations.literal: Jiezan was afraid and begged for an alliance; the emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan grew fearful and sued for peace; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃遣將論頰熱甘辭請於燧，且重幣申勤勤。

translations.literal: He then sent the general Lun Binre with earnest words to request of Sui, and moreover heavy gifts to press his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the general Lun Binre with humble pleas to Sui and rich gifts to press his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 明年，燧還太原，與論頰熱俱朝，盛言宜許以盟，天子然之。

translations.literal: The next year Sui returned to Taiyuan and came to court together with Lun Binre, strongly urging that an alliance ought to be granted; the Son of Heaven agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Sui returned to Taiyuan and came to court with Lun Binre, urging strongly that peace be granted — and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 燧之朝，結贊遽引去。

translations.literal: When Sui came to court, Jiezan abruptly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: While Sui was at court, Jiezan abruptly pulled his army back.

sentences.zh: 帝詔渾瑊與盟平涼，虜劫瑊，僅得免。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Hun Jian to ally at Pingliang; the barbarians ambushed Jian, who barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Hun Jian to treat at Pingliang; the Tibetans ambushed him, and he barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃歸燧之兄子弇，曰：「河曲之屯，春草未生，吾馬饑，公若度河，我無種矣。

translations.literal: The Tibetans returned Sui's elder brother's son Yan and said: "Our encampment on the river bend — spring grass has not yet sprouted and our horses are hungry; if Your Lordship crosses the river we shall have no seed left."
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans returned Sui's nephew Yan with a message: "Our camps on the bend of the Yellow River — the spring grass is not yet up and our horses are starving. Had you crossed the river, we would have been wiped out."

sentences.zh: 賴公許和，今釋弇以報。

translations.literal: We rely on Your Lordship's granting peace; now we release Yan in return.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to your agreeing to peace, we release Yan in return."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞，悔怒，奪其兵，拜司徒，兼侍中，賜妓樂，奉朝請而已。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he regretted and was angry, stripped him of his troops, appointed him Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Attendant, bestowed singing girls and music, and he attended court only as a formality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard this, flushed with anger and regret, stripped him of command, made him Minister of Education and Palace Attendant, gave him musicians and courtesans, and left him a courtier in name only.

sentences.zh: 與李晟皆圖像淩煙閣。

translations.literal: He and Li Sheng both had their portraits placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Sheng were both enshrined with portraits in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 後病足，不任謁。

translations.literal: Later he fell ill in the feet and could not attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: Later illness in his feet kept him from court audiences.

sentences.zh: 九年十月，自力朝延英，詔毋拜。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year he forced himself to attend at Yanying Hall; an edict ordered that he need not bow.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year he dragged himself to Yanying Hall; the emperor excused him from bowing.

sentences.zh: 時晟已卒，帝顧燧曰：「尚記與太尉晟俱來邪？

translations.literal: Li Sheng had already died; the emperor turned to Sui and said: "Do you still remember coming together with Grand Marshal Sheng?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng was already dead; the emperor turned to Sui and said, "Do you still remember coming to court with Grand Marshal Sheng?"

sentences.zh: 今乃獨見公。

translations.literal: Now I see only you alone.
translations.idiomatic: Now I see you alone."

sentences.zh: 」因悲涕。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 燧亦疾而僕，帝親掖之，詔左右扶去，送至陛，燧頓首泣謝。

translations.literal: Sui was also ill and prostrate; the emperor personally supported him, ordered attendants to help him away, escorted him to the steps; Sui knocked his head and wept in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Sui too was ill and could barely stand; the emperor steadied him with his own hands, had attendants help him away, walked him to the steps, and Sui kowtowed in tears of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 固乞骸，讓侍中，不許。

translations.literal: He firmly begged to retire on grounds of infirmity and yield the Palace Attendant post; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He begged repeatedly to retire and yield the Palace Attendant title; the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十，贈太傅，諡曰莊武。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy; posthumously honored as Grand Tutor; posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and given the temple name Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 子匯、暢。

translations.literal: His sons were Hui and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Hui and Chang.

sentences.zh: 子 暢暢少以廕至鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Son Chang — Chang in his youth reached Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations by yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang — in youth Chang rose by yin privilege to Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations.

sentences.zh: 建中中，燧討賊山東，暢留京師。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era Sui campaigned against rebels in the east; Chang remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianzhong, while Sui campaigned in the east, Chang stayed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 於是大旱，朝廷議括商旅緡錢，多亡命入南山為盜。

translations.literal: There was then a great drought; the court debated seizing merchants' and travelers' cash; many fugitives fled into the southern mountains and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought struck; the court debated seizing merchants' cash reserves, and many desperate men fled into the southern hills as bandits.

sentences.zh: 暢客單超俊、李雲端等竊議，以為事且危。

translations.literal: Chang's retainers Shan Chaojun, Li Yunduan and others privately discussed and judged that matters would soon be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's clients Shan Chaojun, Li Yunduan, and others whispered among themselves that disaster was near.

sentences.zh: 暢是其言，遣奴諫燧班師。

translations.literal: Chang agreed with their words and sent a slave to advise Sui to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Chang believed them and sent a servant to urge Sui to withdraw his army.

sentences.zh: 燧怒，執奴以聞，使兄炫拘暢請罪。

translations.literal: Sui was angry, seized the slave and reported it, and had his elder brother Xuan detain Chang to request punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was furious, seized the servant and reported the matter, and had his brother Xuan detain Chang to answer for it.

sentences.zh: 帝方倚燧，貸不問，但誅其客，敕炫賜暢杖三十，然亦罷括商人令。

translations.literal: The emperor was then relying on Sui and pardoned without inquiry, but only executed his clients; he ordered Xuan to grant Chang thirty strokes of the staff, yet also abolished the order to seize merchants' funds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still depended on Sui and spared Chang further punishment, executing only his clients; he ordered Xuan to give Chang thirty strokes of the staff, and dropped the plan to seize merchants' wealth.

sentences.zh: 燧沒後，以貲甲天下，暢亦善殖財，家益豐。

translations.literal: After Sui's death their wealth ranked first under Heaven; Chang was also skilled at multiplying wealth and the household grew still richer.
translations.idiomatic: After Sui's death the family wealth was said to be the greatest in the realm; Chang too was adept at piling up riches, and the house grew still wealthier.

sentences.zh: 晚為豪幸牟侵，又匯妻訟析產。

translations.literal: In his later years powerful favorites encroached for profit, and Hui's wife sued to divide the estate.
translations.idiomatic: In later years powerful favorites preyed on him, and his brother Hui's wife sued to split the family property.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，神策中尉楊志廉諷使納田產。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan the Shence Army vice-commissioner Yang Zhilian hinted that he should turn over land and property.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Zhenyuan, Shence vice-commissioner Yang Zhilian hinted that he should surrender land and estates.

sentences.zh: 至順宗時，復賜之。

translations.literal: When Shunzong came to the throne it was bestowed back to him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzong it was returned to him.

sentences.zh: 中官往往逼取，暢畏不敢吝，以至困窮。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs repeatedly pressed to seize from him; Chang feared and dared not be stingy, until he was reduced to poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs repeatedly extorted from him; Chang was too afraid to refuse, until he was ruined.

sentences.zh: 終少府監，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He ended as Supervisor of the Palace Storehouses; posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Supervisor of the Palace Storehouses and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 諸子無室廬自托。

translations.literal: His sons had no houses or cottages to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were left without homes of their own.

sentences.zh: 奉誠園亭觀，即其安邑裏舊第雲，故當世視暢以厚畜為戒。

translations.literal: The Fengcheng Garden pavilion and viewing hall were said to be his old residence in Anyi Lane; therefore the age took Chang's vast accumulation as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengcheng Garden estate was said to be his old mansion in Anyi Lane — and his fate became a byword against hoarding wealth.

sentences.zh: 有司諡曰縱。

translations.literal: The authorities gave the posthumous title Zong (Licentious).
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him the posthumous name Zong — "Licentious."

sentences.zh: 子繼祖，生四歲以門功為太子舍人，五遷至殿中少監。

translations.literal: His son Jizu at age four was made Crown Prince Attendant by family merit; through five promotions he reached Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jizu, at four, was made Crown Prince Attendant on the family's merit and rose through five promotions to Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 兄 炫燧兄炫，字弱翁。

translations.literal: Elder brother Xuan — Sui's elder brother Xuan, styled Ruoweng.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xuan, styled Ruoweng.

sentences.zh: 少以儒學聞，隱蘇門山，不應辟召。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for classical learning, hid on Mount Sumen, and did not respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was known for scholarship, retired to Mount Sumen, and refused every summons.

sentences.zh: 至德中，李光弼鎮太原，始署掌書記，常參軍謀，光弼器焉。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era Li Guangbi held Taiyuan and first appointed him chief secretary, regularly consulting him on strategy; Guangbi valued him.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhide, when Li Guangbi held Taiyuan, he made Xuan his chief secretary and relied on him in counsel — Guangbi thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中田神功帥宣武，署節度判官，授連、潤二州刺史，以清白顯。

translations.literal: When Tian Shengong of the Ministry of Justice commanded Xuanwu he appointed him military governor's judge, granted him the prefectures of Lian and Run, and he was distinguished for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Shengong commanded Xuanwu he made Xuan his chief administrator, then prefect of Lian and Run, winning fame for spotless conduct.

sentences.zh: 燧為司徒，授刑部侍郎，辭疾，以兵部尚書致仕，卒。

translations.literal: When Sui became Minister of Education he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice; he declined on grounds of illness, retired as Minister of War, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui became Minister of Education, Xuan was named Vice Minister of Justice; pleading illness, he retired as Minister of War and died.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊渾瑊，本鐵勒九姓之渾部也。

translations.literal: Hun Jian — Hun Jian was originally of the Hun clan among the nine surnames of the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian was descended from the Hun clan of the Tiele confederation's nine tribes.

sentences.zh: 世為皋蘭都督。

translations.literal: For generations they served as governors of Gaolan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had held the Gaolan command.

sentences.zh: 父釋之，有才武，從朔方軍，積戰多，遷累開府儀同三司、試太常卿、甯朔郡王。

translations.literal: His father Shizhi had talent in civil and military affairs, followed the Shuofang army, accumulated many battles, and through successive promotions reached Grand General with Extraordinary Honors, Acting Minister of Ceremonies, and King of Ningshuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shizhi was gifted in arms and statecraft, served with the Shuofang army through countless campaigns, and rose to Grand General with Extraordinary Honors, Acting Minister of Ceremonies, and King of Ningshuo.

sentences.zh: 廣德中與吐蕃戰沒。

translations.literal: In the Guangde era he died fighting the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed fighting the Tibetans in the Guangde era.

sentences.zh: 瑊年十一，善騎射，隨釋之防秋，朔方節度使張齊丘戲曰：「與乳媼俱來邪？

translations.literal: Jian at age eleven was skilled in riding and archery; following Shizhi on autumn defense, Shuofang military governor Zhang Qiqiu jested: "Did you come with your wet nurse?"
translations.idiomatic: At eleven Jian was already skilled in riding and archery; on an autumn campaign with his father, Shuofang governor Zhang Qiqiu teased him: "Did you bring your nursemaid along?"

sentences.zh: 」是歲立跳蕩功。

translations.literal: That year he was credited with valor in the assault corps.
translations.idiomatic: That year he won credit in the assault corps.

sentences.zh: 後二年，從破賀魯部，拔石堡城、龍駒島，其勇常冠軍。

translations.literal: Two years later he followed in defeating the Helu tribe, captured Shibao Fortress and Longju Island, and his courage constantly led the army.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he helped crush the Helu tribe, took Shibao Fortress and Longju Island, and his bravery routinely led the field.

sentences.zh: 署折沖果毅。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of a shock-corps unit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of a frontier shock unit.

sentences.zh: 節度使安思順授瑊偏師，入葛祿部，略特羅斯山，破阿布思，與諸軍城永清及天安軍。

translations.literal: Military governor An Sishun gave Jian a detached force; he entered the Gelu tribes, overran Mount Teluosi, defeated Abu Si, and with the armies fortified Yongqing and the Tian'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Governor An Sishun gave him a detached column; he raided deep into Gelu territory, overran Mount Teluosi, defeated Abu Si, and helped build the fortresses at Yongqing and Tian'an.

sentences.zh: 遷中郎將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the household guard.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，從李光弼定河北，射賊驍將李立節，貫其左肩，死之。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled he followed Li Guangbi to pacify Hebei, shot the rebel fierce general Li Lijie, pierced his left shoulder, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled he served under Li Guangbi in Hebei, shot the rebel champion Li Lijie through the left shoulder, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，瑊以兵趨行在。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne Jian led troops to hurry to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong came to the throne, Jian marched his troops to join the emperor in exile.

sentences.zh: 至天德，與虜軍遇，敗之。

translations.literal: Reaching Tiande he met the barbarian army and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: At Tiande he met the enemy and routed them.

sentences.zh: 從郭子儀復兩京，討安慶緒，勝之新鄉，擢武鋒軍使。

translations.literal: He followed Guo Ziyi in recovering the two capitals, campaigned against An Qingxu, defeated him at Xinxiang, and was promoted commander of the Martial Vanguard Army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Ziyi in retaking the capitals, defeated An Qingxu at Xinxiang, and was made commander of the Martial Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 從僕固懷恩平史朝義，大小數十戰，功最，改太常卿，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: He followed Pugu Huai'en in pacifying Shi Chaoyi; in several dozen battles large and small his merit was foremost; he was changed to Minister of Ceremonies with a substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Pugu Huai'en against Shi Chaoyi through dozens of battles and led in merit; he was made Minister of Ceremonies with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 懷恩反，瑊以所部歸子儀，會釋之喪，起復朔方行營兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Huai'en rebelled Jian brought his command back to Guo Ziyi; coinciding with Shizhi's mourning he was recalled from mourning as Shuofang campaign army messenger.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en rebelled, Jian returned to Guo Ziyi with his troops; on his father's death he was recalled from mourning as Shuofang army messenger.

sentences.zh: 從子儀擊吐蕃邠州，留屯邠。

translations.literal: He followed Guo Ziyi in striking the Tibetans at Binzhou and was left to garrison Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Ziyi against the Tibetans at Bin and was left to garrison the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 虜復入，至奉天，瑊戰漠谷，有功，遷太子賓客，屯奉天。

translations.literal: The barbarians entered again and reached Fengtian; Jian fought at Mogu Valley with merit, was promoted to Household Companion of the Heir Apparent, and garrisoned Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans struck again as far as Fengtian, Jian fought them at Mogu Valley with distinction, was made Companion to the Heir Apparent, and garrisoned Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 周智光反，子儀令瑊以步騎萬人下同州。

translations.literal: When Zhou Zhiguang rebelled Guo Ziyi ordered Jian with ten thousand foot and horse down to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Zhiguang rebelled, Guo Ziyi sent Jian with ten thousand foot and horse against Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 智光平，以邠甯隸朔方軍，瑊屯宜祿。

translations.literal: When Zhiguang was pacified Bin and Ning were placed under the Shuofang army; Jian garrisoned Yilu.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiguang's defeat, Bin-Ning was attached to Shuofang command, and Jian garrisoned Yilu.

sentences.zh: 大曆七年，吐蕃盜塞深入，瑊會涇原節度使馬璘討之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali the Tibetans raided the frontier and penetrated deep; Jian joined Jingyuan military governor Ma Lin to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dali the Tibetans broke through the frontier in a deep raid; Jian joined Ma Lin of Jingyuan to drive them back.

sentences.zh: 次黃菩原，瑊引眾據險，設槍壘自營，遏賊奔突。

translations.literal: They encamped at Huangpuyuan; Jian led the masses to hold difficult ground, set up spear ramparts for his own camp, and checked the enemy's charges.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangpuyuan Jian took the high ground, threw up spear palisades around his camp, and blocked the enemy's charges.

sentences.zh: 舊將史抗等內輕瑊，顧左右去槍，叱騎馳賊。

translations.literal: The veteran generals Shi Kang and others inwardly looked down on Jian, glanced to their attendants to remove the spears, and shouted for the cavalry to charge the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Veterans such as Shi Kang secretly despised Jian, ordered the palisades torn down, and drove the cavalry straight at the enemy.

sentences.zh: 既還，虜躡而入，遂大敗，死者十八。

translations.literal: When they returned the barbarians pursued and entered; they were utterly defeated; eight in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: On the retreat the Tibetans pressed in and routed them; eight men in ten were lost.

sentences.zh: 子儀召諸將曰：「朔方軍高天下，今敗於虜，奈何？

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi summoned the generals and said: "The Shuofang army towers over all under Heaven — now defeated by the barbarians, what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi called his generals together: "The Shuofang army has no peer under Heaven — and now the Tibetans have broken us. What do we do?"

sentences.zh: 」瑊曰：「願再戰。

translations.literal: Jian said: "I wish to fight again."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Give me another fight."

sentences.zh: 」乃馳朝那，與鹽州刺史李國臣趨秦原。

translations.literal: He then galloped to Chaona and with Yanzhou prefect Li Guochen hurried to Qinyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to Chaona and, with Yanzhou prefect Li Guochen, raced for Qinyuan.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃引去，瑊邀擊破之，悉奪所掠而還。

translations.literal: The Tibetans withdrew; Jian intercepted and defeated them, recovered all they had plundered, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: As the Tibetans withdrew, Jian ambushed and shattered them, recovered all their loot, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 自是歲防長武城盛秋，領邠州刺史。

translations.literal: From this he annually guarded Changwu city in the height of autumn and held the post of prefect of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he guarded Changwu each autumn at the height of the season and served as prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃入方渠、懷安，瑊擊走之。

translations.literal: The Tibetans entered Fangqu and Huai'an; Jian struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans raided Fangqu and Huai'an, Jian drove them off.

sentences.zh: 子儀入朝，留知邠甯慶兵馬後務。

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi entered court Jian was left to manage the rear affairs of Bin-Ning-Qing troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi went to court, Jian was left in charge of Bin-Ning-Qing logistics.

sentences.zh: 回紇侵太原，破鮑防軍。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs invaded Taiyuan and defeated Bao Fang's army.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs invaded Taiyuan and routed Bao Fang's army.

sentences.zh: 拜瑊都知兵馬使，自石嶺關而南，督諸軍掎角，虜引去。

translations.literal: Jian was appointed overall commander of troops and horses; from Shiling Pass southward he supervised the armies in mutual support; the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was made overall commander of cavalry and infantry; south from Shiling Pass he coordinated the armies in mutual support until the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進兼單于副都護、振武軍使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to concurrent Vice Protector-General of the Chanyu and commander of the Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was further named Vice Protector-General of the Chanyu and commander of the Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 子儀為太尉，德宗析所部為三節度，以瑊兼單于大都護，振武、東受降城、鎮北大都護府、綏銀麟勝州節度副大使。

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi became Grand Marshal, Dezong divided his command into three military governorships; Jian was made concurrent Grand Protector-General of the Chanyu, deputy military governor of Zhenwu, Eastern Surrender City, the Northern Pacification Protectorate, and Sui-Yin-Lin-Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi became Grand Marshal, Dezong split his domain into three commands; Jian was named Grand Protector-General of the Chanyu and deputy governor over Zhenwu, the surrender cities, the northern protectorate, and Sui-Yin-Lin-Sheng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，崔甯領朔方，故召為左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long Cui Ning took Shuofang; he was therefore recalled as great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cui Ning took over Shuofang, and Jian was recalled as great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 建中中，李希烈詐為瑊書，若同亂者，帝識其諜，用不疑，更賜良馬、錦幣。

translations.literal: In Jianzhong Li Xilie forged a letter in Jian's name as if he were joining the rebellion; the emperor recognized the spy craft and used him without doubt, further bestowing fine horses and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianzhong, Li Xilie forged a letter in Jian's name implicating him in rebellion; the emperor saw through the ruse, trusted him all the more, and gave him fine horses and silks.

sentences.zh: 普王為荊襄元帥討希烈也，以瑊為中軍都虞候。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Pu was supreme commander of Jing-Xiang to suppress Xilie, Jian was made chief adjutant of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Pu led the Jing-Xiang campaign against Xilie, Jian served as chief adjutant of the center.

sentences.zh: 帝狩奉天，瑊率家人子弟以從，授行在都虞候、京畿渭北節度使。

translations.literal: When the emperor hunted at Fengtian Jian led family members and sons to follow; he was appointed chief adjutant at the imperial camp and military governor of the capital district and north of Wei.
