translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Fengtian, Jian brought his kin and household troops with him and was named chief adjutant at court and military governor of the capital approaches north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 硃泚兵薄城，戰譙門，晨至日中不解。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's troops pressed the city; they fought at the watchtower gate from morning until midday without respite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's army pressed the walls; at the watchtower gate the battle raged from dawn until noon without pause.

sentences.zh: 或以芻車至，瑊曳車塞門，焚以戰，賊乃解。

translations.literal: When fodder carts arrived Jian dragged the carts to block the gate, burned them to fight, and the rebels then lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When fodder carts arrived, Jian dragged them to block the gate, set them ablaze as a barrier, and the rebels broke off.

sentences.zh: 泚治攻具，矢石四集如雨，晝夜不息，凡浹日，鑿塹圜城。

translations.literal: Ci prepared siege engines; arrows and stones gathered from four sides like rain, day and night without cease, for many days in succession, digging trenches to encircle the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ci built siege engines; arrows and stones fell like rain from every side, day and night without cease for days on end, while his men dug trenches to ring the city.

sentences.zh: 城中死者可藉，人心危惴，或夜縋出掇蔬本供禦，帝與瑊相泣。

translations.literal: The dead in the city could be piled layer upon layer; hearts were perilous with fear; some at night were lowered by rope to gather vegetable roots for the imperial table; the emperor and Jian wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: The dead in the city lay in heaps; panic gripped every heart; some were lowered by rope at night to gather wild greens for the emperor's table — and the emperor and Jian wept together.

sentences.zh: 泚方據乾陵下瞰城，翠翟紅袍，左右宦人趨走，宴賜拜舞，又縱慢辭戲斥天子，以為勝在景刻。

translations.literal: Ci was just then holding Qianling overlooking the city in kingfisher-feather crown and red robe, eunuchs hurrying left and right, feasting and bestowing gifts with bowing dances; he also let loose insolent words mocking the Son of Heaven, thinking victory was within a moment's reach.
translations.idiomatic: Ci held Qianling overlooking the city in imperial green and crimson, eunuchs scurrying at his side, feasting and dispensing rewards while his men danced obeisance — and he hurled insults at the emperor, sure that victory was only hours away.

sentences.zh: 使騎環馳，責大臣不識天命。

translations.literal: He sent horsemen circling and galloping, reproaching the great ministers for not recognizing Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He sent horsemen circling the walls to berate the ministers for failing to read Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 造雲梁，廣數十丈，施大輪，濡氈及革冒之，周布水囊為鄣，指城東北；

translations.literal: He built a cloud-bridge several tens of paces wide, fitted with great wheels, covered with soaked felt and leather, with water bags arrayed all around as ramparts, aimed at the northeast of the city;
translations.idiomatic: He built a siege tower tens of paces wide on great wheels, sheathed in wet felt and leather, ringed with water bags as a fire screen, and aimed it at the northeast corner;

sentences.zh: 構木廬，蒙革周置之，運薪土其下，將塞隍。

translations.literal: he constructed wooden sheds, wrapped in leather placed all around, hauling firewood and earth beneath, intending to fill the moat.
translations.idiomatic: and threw up wooden sheds wrapped in hides, hauling brush and earth beneath to fill the moat.

sentences.zh: 帝召瑊，授以詔書千余，自御史大夫、實封五百戶而下，募突將死士當賊，賜瑊筆，使量功署詔，不足則署衣以授，因曰：「朕與公訣矣，令馬承倩往，有急可奏。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Jian and gave him more than a thousand edicts, from Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and a substantive fief of five hundred households downward, to recruit shock troops and death-defying warriors to meet the enemy; he bestowed Jian a brush to grant edicts according to merit, and if insufficient then to inscribe on garments and grant; he then said: "I take leave of you; I send Ma Chengqian — if there is urgency you may memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Jian in and gave him a thousand blank patents — from Vice Director of the Secretariat and five-hundred-household fiefs on down — to reward shock troops who would face the enemy. He gave Jian his brush to sign commissions by merit, and when the edicts ran out, to write on robes instead. "I bid you farewell," the emperor said. "Ma Chengqian will carry word — report any crisis at once."

sentences.zh: 」瑊俯伏嗚咽，帝撫而遣之。

translations.literal: Jian prostrated himself sobbing; the emperor comforted him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Jian prostrated himself, sobbing; the emperor comforted him and sent him out.

sentences.zh: 瑊前與防城使侯仲莊揣雲梁所道，掘大隧，積馬矢及薪然之。

translations.literal: Earlier Jian with city-defense commissioner Hou Zhongzhuang estimated the cloud-bridge's route, dug a great tunnel, piled horse dung and firewood and set them burning.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and city-defense commissioner Hou Zhongzhuang had guessed the tower's path, dug a great tunnel, and piled horse dung and brush to burn.

sentences.zh: 賊乘風推梁以進，載數千人。

translations.literal: The rebels rode the wind to push the bridge forward, carrying several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pushed the tower forward on the wind, thousands of men aboard.

sentences.zh: 王師乘城者皆凍餒，甲弊兵盬，瑊但以忠義感率使當賊，人憂不支，群臣號天以禱。

translations.literal: The imperial troops on the walls were all frozen and starving, armor worn and weapons blunt; Jian could only move them with loyalty and righteousness to meet the enemy; men feared they could not hold; the ministers cried to Heaven in prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders on the walls were frozen, starving, in rotting armor with dulled blades; Jian could only rally them by appeal to loyalty and duty; men feared the line would break; ministers cried to Heaven in prayer.

sentences.zh: 瑊中矢，自揠去，被血而戰愈厲。

translations.literal: Jian was struck by an arrow, pulled it out himself, drenched in blood yet fought all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Jian took an arrow, pulled it out himself, and fought on all the fiercer, drenched in blood.

sentences.zh: 雲梁及隧而陷，風返悉焚，賊皆死，舉城歡噪。

translations.literal: The cloud-bridge reached the tunnel and sank; the wind turned and all was burned; the rebels all died; the whole city shouted in joy.
translations.idiomatic: The tower reached the tunnel and collapsed; the wind shifted and the blaze consumed it; the attackers perished; the whole city erupted in cheers.

sentences.zh: 是日詔授瑊二子官，乃第賞將校。

translations.literal: That day an edict granted offices to Jian's two sons; then rewards were ranked for officers and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor ennobled Jian's two sons and ranked rewards for his officers.

sentences.zh: 泚攻城益急，會李懷光奔難，賊乃去。

translations.literal: Ci pressed the siege ever harder; when Li Huai'guang came to the rescue the rebels then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ci pressed the attack harder still — until Li Huai'guang marched to the rescue and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進行在都知兵馬使，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to overall commander of troops and horses at the imperial camp with a substantive fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted overall commander at the imperial camp with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 乘輿進狩山南，瑊以諸軍衛入穀口，懷光追騎至，後軍擊卻之。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage advanced to hunt in the southern mountains; Jian with the armies guarded the valley mouth; Huai'guang's pursuing cavalry arrived and the rear guard struck and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor fled south into the hills, Jian guarded the valley mouth with the army; when Huai'guang's pursuit caught up, the rearguard beat them back.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事，兼靈鹽豐夏定遠西城天德軍節度、朔方邠甯振武道永平軍奉天行營副元帥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrently military governor of Ling, Yan, Feng, Xia, Dingyuan, Western City, and Tiande armies, and deputy supreme commander of the Shuofang, Bin-Ning, Zhenwu circuit, Yongping Army, and Fengtian campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Left Vice Director, Grand Councilor, military governor over the northwestern commands, and deputy supreme commander of the Fengtian campaign and the Shuofang-Bin-Ning-Zhenwu frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝臨軒授鉞，用漢拜韓信故事，制曰：「寇賊幹紀，授爾節鉞，以戡多難，往欽哉！

translations.literal: The emperor at the hall bestowed the battle-axe, using the Han precedent of enfeoffing Han Xin, with an edict saying: "Bandits and rebels violate the age — I grant you staff and axe to quell many calamities; go and take reverent heed!"
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor invested him with the battle-axe, following the Han precedent of enfeoffing Han Xin: "Rebels defy Heaven's order — I give you command to crush this calamity. Go, and be worthy of it!"

sentences.zh: 」瑊頓首曰：「敢不畢力以對揚天子休命？

translations.literal: Jian knocked his head and said: "How dare I not exhaust my strength to respond to and proclaim the Son of Heaven's gracious command?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian kowtowed and said, "How dare I not give my all to answer the emperor's gracious trust?"

sentences.zh: 」乃率諸軍趨京師。

translations.literal: He then led the armies toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Then he led the armies toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 賊韓旻拒武功，瑊率吐蕃論莽羅兵破之武亭川，斬首萬級，遂屯奉天，以抗西面。

translations.literal: The rebel Han Min held Wugong; Jian led Tibetan Lun Mangluo's troops and defeated him at Wutingchuan, cut ten thousand heads, then encamped at Fengtian to resist the western front.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Han Min held Wugong; Jian led Tibetan allies under Lun Mangluo and routed him at Wutingchuan, taking ten thousand heads, then encamped at Fengtian to hold the western approach.

sentences.zh: 李晟自東渭橋破賊，瑊與韓游瑰、戴休顏以西軍收咸陽，進屯延秋門。

translations.literal: Li Sheng from the eastern Wei Bridge broke the rebels; Jian with Han Yougui and Dai Xiuyan with the western army recovered Xianyang and advanced to encamp at Yanqiu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng broke the rebels from the eastern Wei Bridge; Jian, Han Yougui, and Dai Xiuyan swept in from the west, retook Xianyang, and encamped at Yanqiu Gate.

sentences.zh: 泚平，論功，以瑊兼侍中，實封戶八百。

translations.literal: When Ci was pacified merit was discussed; Jian was made concurrent Palace Attendant with a substantive fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci was crushed, Jian was made Palace Attendant with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天子還宮，授河中絳慈隰節度使、河中同陝虢行營副元帥，繇樓煩郡王徙咸寧；

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace he was appointed military governor of Hezhong, Jiang, Ci, and Xi, and deputy supreme commander of the Hezhong-Tong-Shaan-Guo campaign; he moved from King of Loufan commandery to Xianning;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, Jian was made military governor of Hezhong, Jiang, Ci, and Xi and deputy commander of the eastern campaign; his title shifted from King of Loufan to Xianning;

sentences.zh: 賜大寧裏甲第，女樂五人，將相送歸第，與李晟鈞禮。

translations.literal: bestowed a mansion in Daning Lane, five female musicians; generals and ministers escorted him home; he received equal ceremony with Li Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: and was given a mansion in Daning Lane, five musicians, and an escort home by the court's highest officers — honors equal to Li Sheng's.

sentences.zh: 俄加朔方行營副元帥，與馬燧同討李懷光。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made deputy supreme commander of the Shuofang campaign and joined Ma Sui in suppressing Li Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named deputy commander of the Shuofang campaign and joined Ma Sui against Li Huai'guang.

sentences.zh: 懷光平，檢校司空，任一子五品官。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang was pacified he was made acting Minister of Works and one son was granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang fell, Jian was made acting Minister of Works and one son received a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 還屯河中。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to garrison Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃相尚結贊陷鹽、夏，陰窺京師，而畏瑊與李晟、馬燧，欲以計勝之。

translations.literal: The Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan captured Yan and Xia, secretly eyed the capital, yet feared Jian together with Li Sheng and Ma Sui, and wished to overcome them by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan held Yan and Xia and watched the capital, but feared Jian, Li Sheng, and Ma Sui — and sought to defeat them by guile.

sentences.zh: 乃詭辭重禮，請燧講好，燧苦贊，帝乃詔約盟平涼川，以瑊為會盟使。

translations.literal: He therefore used deceitful words and heavy gifts to request peace talks with Sui; Sui importuned Jiezan; the emperor then ordered alliance at Pingliangchuan and appointed Jian as alliance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He sent honeyed words and rich gifts to coax Sui into peace talks; Sui pressed for an accord; the court agreed to treaty at Pingliangchuan and named Jian the envoy.

sentences.zh: 為結贊所劫，副使崔漢衡以下皆陷，惟瑊得免。

translations.literal: He was seized by Jiezan; deputy envoy Cui Hanheng and those below were all trapped; only Jian escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan ambushed the party; deputy Cui Hanheng and the rest were taken, but Jian alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 自奉天入朝，羸服待罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: From Fengtian he entered court in worn garments awaiting punishment; an edict released him.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court from Fengtian in humble dress to await judgment; the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃復入盜，使瑊鎮奉天。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans again entered to raid he was sent to hold Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans raided again, he was sent to hold Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 虜罷，還河中。

translations.literal: When the barbarians ceased he returned to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders withdrew, he returned to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，虜入涇、邠，授邠甯慶副元帥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan the barbarians entered Jing and Bin; he was appointed deputy supreme commander of Bin-Ning-Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, when the enemy struck Jing and Bin, he was named deputy commander of Bin-Ning-Qing.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司徒，兼中書令。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting Minister of Education and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted acting Minister of Education and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十五年卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 群臣奉慰延英，贈太師，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: The ministers offered condolences at Yanying Hall; he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor; posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers offered condolences at Yanying Hall; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the temple name Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 喪車至自鎮，帝復廢朝。

translations.literal: When the funeral carriage arrived from his command the emperor again suspended court.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral train arrived from his command, the emperor again suspended court.

sentences.zh: 瑊好書，通《春秋》、《漢書》。

translations.literal: Jian loved books and was versed in the "Spring and Autumn Annals" and the "Book of Han."
translations.idiomatic: Jian loved learning and was versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 嘗慕《司馬遷自敘》，著《行紀》一篇，其辭一不矜大。

translations.literal: He once admired Sima Qian's "Autobiographical Postface" and composed one piece, "Record of Conduct," whose wording never once boasted.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Sima Qian's autobiographical postface and wrote a "Record of Conduct" whose tone never once swaggered.

sentences.zh: 天性忠謹，功高而志益下，歲時貢奉，必躬閱視。

translations.literal: By nature loyal and careful, though his merit was high his will grew ever lower; seasonal tribute he always personally inspected.
translations.idiomatic: By nature loyal and scrupulous, he grew humbler as his achievements mounted; he personally inspected every item of seasonal tribute.

sentences.zh: 每有賜予，下拜跽受，常若在帝前，世方之金日磾，故帝終始信待。

translations.literal: Whenever there were grants he bowed and knelt to receive them, always as if before the emperor; the age compared him to Jin Midi; therefore the emperor trusted and treated him from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor gave him anything, he knelt to receive it as if in the throne room itself; men compared him to Jin Midi, and the emperor trusted him to the end.

sentences.zh: 貞元後，天子常恐籓侯生事，稍桀驁則姑息之，惟瑊有所奏論不盡從可，輒私喜曰：「上不疑我。

translations.literal: After Zhenyuan the Son of Heaven constantly feared that regional lords would stir trouble; if slightly defiant they were indulged; only when Jian had some memorial or discussion not entirely followed would he privately rejoice, saying: "The sovereign does not doubt me."
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenyuan the emperor feared trouble from the regional lords and indulged any who grew defiant — so whenever the throne did not adopt every point of Jian's advice, he would privately rejoice: "The emperor still does not doubt me."

sentences.zh: 」故治蒲十六年，常持軍，猜間不能入。

translations.literal: Therefore he governed Pu for sixteen years, constantly holding troops; suspicion could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Pu for sixteen years, always keeping his army ready — and no whisper of suspicion could touch him.

sentences.zh: 君子賢之。

translations.literal: Men of worth esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 本名日進，稍顯改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Rijin; when he became prominent it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Rijin; he changed it when he rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 五子，鎬、鐬為達官。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Gao and Hui became eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons; Gao and Hui rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 子 鎬鎬謙謹，喜交士大夫，曆鄧、唐二州刺史，有政譽。

translations.literal: Son Gao — Gao was modest and careful, delighted in associating with scholar-officials, served successively as prefect of Deng and Tang, and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao was modest and careful, cultivated ties with scholar-officials, served as prefect of Deng and Tang in turn, and won a name for sound administration.

sentences.zh: 元和中，延州沙陀部苦邊吏貪，震擾不安。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era the Shatuo tribes of Yanzhou suffered from the greed of frontier officers and were shaken and disturbed without peace.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe the Shatuo of Yanzhou groaned under corrupt frontier officers and grew restless.

sentences.zh: 李絳建言，宜選才職稱者為刺史。

translations.literal: Li Jiang offered counsel that one ought to select someone whose talent matched the post as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang advised appointing a prefect whose ability matched the post.

sentences.zh: 乃任鎬延州。

translations.literal: Gao was therefore appointed to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was given Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會討王承宗，而義武節度使任迪簡病不能軍，以鎬將家可用，乃遷檢校右散騎常侍、義武軍節度副使，俄代迪簡為使。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Wang Chengzong, Yiwu military governor Ren Dijian was ill and could not command the army; because Gao's general family was usable he was transferred to acting Right Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and deputy military governor of the Yiwu Army, and soon replaced Dijian as governor.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wang Chengzong, Yiwu governor Ren Dijian fell too ill to command; Gao's martial lineage recommended him, and he was made acting Right Cavalier Attendant and deputy governor of Yiwu, soon replacing Dijian outright.

sentences.zh: 治兵頗有法，然短于計略，不持重。

translations.literal: He drilled troops with considerable method, yet was short in stratagem and not steady in weight.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled his troops well enough, but lacked strategic depth and steady judgment.

sentences.zh: 鎮、定二軍間不百里，鎬引兵壓鎮境而屯，距賊三十里，鼓角聲相聞。

translations.literal: Between the Zhen and Ding armies was less than a hundred li; Gao led troops pressing the Zhen border to encamp, thirty li from the rebels, drums and horns audible to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Ding lay less than a hundred li apart; Gao pressed the Zhen frontier and camped thirty li from the rebels, drums and horns answering across the gap.

sentences.zh: 賊始亦畏，見鎬無斥候，乃潛師入定境，焚廥蓄，屠鄉聚，鎬軍遂搖。

translations.literal: The rebels at first also feared him; seeing Gao had no scouts they secretly moved troops into Ding territory, burned granaries and stores, slaughtered villages and hamlets, and Gao's army then wavered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels feared him at first — until they saw he posted no scouts. They slipped into Ding territory, burned stores, massacred villages, and Gao's army lost its nerve.

sentences.zh: 亦會中人督戰，乃出薄賊，大敗而還。

translations.literal: It also happened that a court eunuch supervised the battle; he then went out to press the rebels, was utterly defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch was also pressing for action; Gao sallied against the rebels, was routed, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 詔以陳楚代之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chen Chu to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced him with Chen Chu.

sentences.zh: 時師饑凍，聞鎬方罷，遂亂，劫鎬之家，至裸辱。

translations.literal: At the time the army was hungry and freezing; hearing Gao had just been dismissed they then mutinied, plundered Gao's household, even to naked humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: The army was starving and freezing; when word spread that Gao had been removed, the troops mutinied, looted his home, and humiliated his family openly.

sentences.zh: 楚聞，馳入城，乃定。

translations.literal: When Chu heard he galloped into the city and then it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Chu galloped into camp on hearing the news and restored order.

sentences.zh: 令軍中斂所剽歸鎬，以兵衛出之。

translations.literal: He ordered the army to gather what had been plundered and return it to Gao, and with troops as escort led him out.
translations.idiomatic: He made the men return what they had stolen to Gao and escorted him out under guard.

sentences.zh: 貶韶州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao was demoted to prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was demoted to prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 後代州刺史韓重華奏收鎬供軍金幣十余萬，乃復貶循州。

translations.literal: Later Yanzhou prefect Han Chonghua memorialized recovering more than a hundred thousand in gold and coin Gao had supplied to the army; he was again demoted to Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yanzhou prefect Han Chonghua reported recovering over a hundred thousand in army funds Gao had held; Gao was demoted again to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子 鐬鐬以廕補諸衛參軍，累擬至豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Son Hui — Hui by yin privilege was made military aide in the guard regiments, and through successive nominations reached prefect of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui entered the guard regiments by yin privilege and rose through nominations to prefect of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐贓七百萬，文宗以勳臣子，貶袁州司馬。

translations.literal: He was convicted of embezzling seven million; Emperor Wenzong because he was a meritorious minister's son demoted him to military aide of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of embezzling seven million, he was spared harsher punishment as a hero's son and demoted to military aide of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 還為袁王傅，至太子詹事。

translations.literal: He returned as tutor to the Prince of Yuan, and reached Household Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as tutor to the Prince of Yuan and rose to Household Steward of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 訓、注亂，或言鐬匿賈餗，為百騎所捕，苦辨乃免，然家為兵剽皆盡。

translations.literal: In the disorder of Xun and Zhu it was said Hui harbored Jia Su; he was seized by the hundred riders, argued strenuously and was spared, yet his household was plundered by troops to the last.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xun-Zhu coup he was accused of sheltering Jia Su, seized by the imperial guard, and cleared only after desperate pleas — but soldiers looted his home bare.

sentences.zh: 文宗憐之，授少府監，遷殿中。

translations.literal: Wenzong pitied him and appointed him Supervisor of the Palace Storehouses; he was transferred to the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong took pity on him, made him Supervisor of the Palace Storehouses, and later moved him into palace service.

sentences.zh: 宰相以瑊之裔，擢刺史，帝曰：「是豈可以牧民？

translations.literal: The chief ministers because he was Jian's descendant promoted him to prefect; the emperor said: "How can such a one shepherd the people?"
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, citing his descent from Hun Jian, proposed him for a prefecture; the emperor said, "How could such a man govern a province?"

sentences.zh: 念其父功，富之可也。

translations.literal: Considering his father's merit, enriching him is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Remember his father's service — enrich him, by all means, but do not put him over people."

sentences.zh: 」宰相言鐬嘗治郡有績，從之，拜夀州刺史。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said Hui had once governed a commandery with achievement; the emperor followed this and appointed him prefect of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers argued that Hui had once governed competently; the emperor relented and named him prefect of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 終諸衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He ended as great general of the guard regiments.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as great general of the guard regiments.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唐史臣稱燧沈雄忠力，常先計後戰。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tang historians call Sui deep, heroic, loyal, and forceful, always planning first and fighting afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Tang historians describe Sui as deep, bold, loyal, and forceful — a commander who always planned before he fought.

sentences.zh: 每戰，親令於眾，無不感概用命，鬥必決死，未嘗折北，名蓋一時。

translations.literal: In every battle he personally issued orders before the masses; none failed to be moved and devote their lives; in combat they were resolved to die; he never suffered defeat; his fame covered an age.
translations.idiomatic: Before every battle he addressed the ranks in person; none failed to answer with fierce devotion; his men fought as if death meant nothing; he never knew defeat, and his fame eclipsed his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 然力能得田悅而不取，虜不可信而決信之，故河北三盜卒不臣，平涼大臣奔辱，燧之罪也。

translations.literal: Yet though his strength could have taken Tian Yue he did not; barbarians could not be trusted yet he firmly trusted them; therefore the three Hebei rebels in the end did not submit, and at Pingliang great ministers fled in disgrace — these are Sui's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he had the power to finish Tian Yue he held back; when the Tibetans had proved untrustworthy he trusted them anyway — so the three Hebei rebels never submitted, and ministers were shamed at Pingliang. These faults are Sui's.

sentences.zh: 雖然，燧賢者也，天下以為可責故責之，不以功掩罪，亦不可以罪廢功。

translations.literal: Even so, Sui was a worthy man; all under Heaven judged him blameworthy and therefore blamed him — one must not let merit cover crimes, nor may crimes abolish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Still, Sui was a man of worth; the world held him to a higher standard and therefore faulted him — merit must not hide fault, but fault must not erase merit.

sentences.zh: 瑊親與結贊盟，不能料虜詐，但以如詔為恭，殆有猛志而無英才乎？

translations.literal: Jian personally allied with Jiezan, could not foresee barbarian deceit, and took mere compliance with the edict as reverence — perhaps he had fierce will but lacked outstanding talent?
translations.idiomatic: Jian treated with Jiezan in person, failed to foresee Tibetan treachery, and mistook obedience to the edict for true loyalty — fierce in spirit, perhaps, but not quite a master?

sentences.zh: 李晟謂虜不可與盟，則燧、瑊固出晟下遠甚。

translations.literal: Li Sheng said barbarians could not be allied with — then Sui and Jian were indeed far below Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng had warned that the Tibetans could not be trusted in treaty — and in that judgment Sui and Jian fell far short of him.

sentences.zh: 功名大小，信其然乎！

translations.literal: Great or small in merit and fame — is it not truly so!
translations.idiomatic: Great fame and small — is it not exactly so!
